Rashi on Ketubot 42b:10:1.hebrew: וכי אמר רבה ממונא הוי להורישו - משעמד בדין, בשאר קנסות, ולא מיפטר תו בהודאה:
Rashi on Ketubot 42b:10:1.english: And when Rabba said [that] it is a monetary obligation to bequeath it - [This refers to] once he has stood trial, regarding other fines, and he is no longer exempt through admission.

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:11:1.hebrew: יתן לחוד ונתן לחוד - יתן משמע לשון צווי ולעולם, ונתן משמע דבר הנתון כבר:
Rashi on Ketubot 42b:11:1.english: “Yiten” is distinct, and “venatan” is distinct - “Yiten” [“he shall give”] implies an expression of command [that applies] at all times, whereas “venatan” [“and he shall give”] implies something already given.

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:12:1.hebrew: אי הכי - דשאני קנס דאונס ומפתה משאר קנסות, דאפילו עמד בדין נמי לאו ממונא הוא:
Rashi on Ketubot 42b:12:1.english: If so - that the fine of a rapist and a seducer differs from other fines, in that even [after] he has stood trial it is still not [considered] money.

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:12:2.hebrew: ת"ל וכחש - בתמיה. כלומר, מאי איריא דנסיב לה הש"ס לפטורא מוכחש כי היכי דיליף שאר קנסות — כלומר, מדלא דמי לתשומת יד למיהוי עיקר תחילתו ממון — תיפוק ליה דהשתא נמי לאו ממונא הוא, דרחמנא אמר ונתן, דלא זיכתה לו תורה עד שעת נתינה:
Rashi on Ketubot 42b:12:2.english: The verse states: "And deal falsely" - [This is said] in astonishment. That is to say: Why does the Talmud specifically derive the exemption from "and deal falsely," just as it derives [the exemption for] other fines — meaning, because it is not similar to a deposit [tesumet yad], whose original essence is monetary — [when] it could derive it from the fact that even now it is not [considered] money, for the Merciful One said "shall give," [teaching] that the Torah did not grant it to him until the time of giving?

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:13:1.hebrew: כי איצטריך וכחש - לקנס דאונס ופתוי, למילפינהו בהדי שאר קנסות לפטורא מוכחש, משום דעיקרן קנס, ולא מצי למילף מונתן:
Rashi on Ketubot 42b:13:1.english: When "and deal falsely" was necessary - [This refers] to the fine of rape and seduction, to derive them along with the other fines for exemption from "and deal falsely," because their essence is a fine, and one cannot derive [it] from "and he shall give."

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:13:2.hebrew: כגון שעמדה בדין ובגרה - דלרבי שמעון דידה הוא, דכי היכי דפליג במתניתין בלא הספיקה לגבות עד שמת האב, הכי נמי פליג בלא הספיקה לגבות עד שבגרה, דקאמר ת"ק: הרי הן של אב, ולרבי שמעון: הרי הוא של עצמה. ואם מתה אחרי כן, ירית לה אביה מכח דידה והוי ממון גמור, ואע"ג דלא מטא לידה, דלגבי דידה לא הוה שאני משאר קנסות, דמשעת העמדה בדין ממונא הוא, וכי מייתא ירית הוא כל זכות שהיה לה בו. הלכך, מונתן לא מצי למיפטריה, ונסיב הש"ס מוכחש, ומשום דעיקרו קנס:
Rashi on Ketubot 42b:13:2.english: Where she stood in judgment and reached majority - For according to Rabbi Shimon, it is hers. For just as he disagrees in the Mishnah regarding [a case where] she did not manage to collect [it] before the father died, so too does he disagree regarding [a case where] she did not manage to collect [it] before she reached majority — where the Tanna Kamma says, "Behold, they belong to the father," and according to Rabbi Shimon, "Behold, it belongs to herself." And if she died afterwards, her father inherits her by virtue of her [ownership], and it is full-fledged money, even though it did not reach her hand. Because with respect to her, it is no different from other fines, since from the time of standing in judgment it is [considered] money, and when she dies, he inherits every right that she had in it. Therefore, one cannot exempt him from [the verse] "and he shall give," and the Talmud derives [it] from [the verse] "and deal falsely," because its origin is a fine.

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:14:1.hebrew: אי הכי - דבשעמד בדין אוקימתה וכבר נעשה ממון, היכי קתני "יצאו אלו שהן קנס"? הא ממון נינהו:
Rashi on Ketubot 42b:14:1.english: If so - Since you have established it [as referring to a case] where he stood in court, and it has already become a monetary [obligation], how does [the baraita] teach, "Excluding these, as they are a fine"? Surely they are monetary [payments]!

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:15:1.hebrew: שאינו משלם קנס כו' - ואי הוה מודי הוה מיפטר, אלמא טעמא דרבי שמעון משום דאי הוה מודי מיפטר הוא. והא ליתא אלא כשלא עמד בדין:
Rashi on Ketubot 42b:15:1.english: As he does not pay a fine, etc. - And if he had confessed, he would have been exempt. Thus, Rabbi Shimon's reason is because if he had confessed, he would have been exempt — and this is only [so] when he has not stood trial.

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:15:2.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: והא עמד בדין, דמשלם <abbr title="על פי">ע"פ</abbr> עצמו, קרבן שבועה נמי מיחייב:
Rashi on Ketubot 42b:15:2.english: This is the reading: "And [if] he stood trial, in which case he pays on his own [admission], he is also liable [to bring] an oath-offering."

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:16:1.english: The Merciful One exempts him - From an oath-offering.

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:16:2.english: From "And deal falsely with his neighbor" - For [Scripture] specified in it only things whose essence is monetary.

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:1:1.hebrew: מאי לאו בשעמד בדין - בב"ד אחד, ובאו עדים באותו ב"ד וחייבוהו ב"ד על פיהם, ועכשיו זה תובעו מה שחייבוהו ב"ד וחזר וכפר, וקתני פטור:
Rashi on Ketubot 42b:1:1.english: What, is it not [referring to a case] where he has stood trial - In one court, and witnesses came in that court and the court obligated him based on their [testimony], and now this [claimant] demands from him what the court obligated him, and he then denied [it], and [the baraita] teaches [that he is] exempt.

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:1:2.english: Where he has not stood trial - And witnesses have not yet testified.

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:2:1.hebrew: והא מדרישא - מילתייהו דרבנן דאיפליגו עליה וחייבוהו קרבן שבועה איירי בשעמד בדין, מכלל דסיפא — כלומר ר"ש דאתא לאיפלוגי עלייהו — בדכוותה איירי:
Rashi on Ketubot 42b:2:1.english: But from [the fact] that the first clause - The statement of the Rabbis, who disagreed with him [Rabbi Shimon] and obligated him [to bring] an oath offering, deals with [a case] where he stood trial; [this] implies that the latter clause — that is, Rabbi Shimon, who comes to disagree with them — deals with a similar [case].

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:2:2.english: I have only - that he becomes liable for principal, a fifth, and a guilt-offering.

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:3:1.hebrew: כפילא מי איכא - מי יימר דגנב, דתבעיה כפילא? ועוד, דלמא מודי ומיפטר:
Rashi on Ketubot 42b:3:1.english: Is there double [payment] - Who says that he stole [it], that he claims double [payment] from him? And furthermore, perhaps he would confess and be exempt.

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:3:2.hebrew: אלא פשיטא בשעמד בדין - והא דקתני יצאו אלו שהן קנס, לקמן מפרש לה, שעיקרן קנס:
Rashi on Ketubot 42b:3:2.english: Rather, [it is] obvious [that it is] where he stood trial - And [as for] that which [the baraita] teaches, "these are excluded, for they are a fine," [the Gemara] explains it below: that their essence is a fine.

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:4:1.hebrew: או ליתני רישא - דכולה "רבי שמעון אומר", או ליתני סיפא כו'. מאי שנא דאיפסיק ותנא "רבי שמעון אומר" בי מיצעי:
Rashi on Ketubot 42b:4:1.english: Or let it teach [in the] first clause - That the entire [baraita is] "Rabbi Shimon says," or let it teach [in the] latter clause, etc. Why is it different that it interrupted and taught "Rabbi Shimon says" in the middle?

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:6:1.hebrew: ומודינא לך לענין קרבן שבועה - דלרבי שמעון, אע"ג דעמד בדין, לא מיחייב עליה קרבן שבועה:
Rashi on Ketubot 42b:6:1.english: And I concede to you with regard to an offering [for] an oath - That according to Rabbi Shimon, even though he stood in court, he is not liable [to bring] an offering [for] an oath for it.

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:7:1.hebrew: להורישו לבניו - משעמד בדין ומת עד שלא הספיק לגבות, הרי הוא של אחיה ולא שלה:
Rashi on Ketubot 42b:7:1.english: To bequeath it to his sons - Once [the perpetrator] stood trial and [the father] died before he managed to collect [it], it belongs to her brothers and not to her.

Rashi on Ketubot 42b:9:1.hebrew: עשרין ותרתין שנין - הן היו ימי שררתו של רבה, ומת וישב רב יוסף בראש, וסייעוהו מן השמים לפרקה להיות לו לשם. לפי שהיה רבה חריף, ולכך קראוהו עוקר הרים; ורב יוסף היה בעל שמועות ומשנה וברייתא, לכך קראוהו סיני:
Rashi on Ketubot 42b:9:1.english: Twenty-two years - These were the years of Rabbah's leadership, and he died, and Rav Yosef sat at the head [of the academy], and they assisted him from Heaven to resolve it so that he would gain renown. For Rabbah was sharp-minded, and therefore they called him "uprooter of mountains"; and Rav Yosef was a master of traditions, Mishnah, and baraita, [and] therefore they called him "Sinai."

Tosafot on Ketubot 42b:11:1.hebrew: ונתן לחוד - וגבי מוציא שם רע, דכתי': "ונתנו לאבי הנערה", איכא למימ': "ונתן" לחוד, "ונתנו" לחוד:
Tosafot on Ketubot 42b:11:1.english: Venatan [shall give] is distinct - And with regard to a defamer [motzi shem ra], where it is written: "And they shall give [venatenu] to the father of the young woman," one can say: "Venatan" is distinct, [and] "venatenu" is distinct.

Tosafot on Ketubot 42b:12:1.hebrew: אי הכי, ת"ל "וכחש"? ת"ל "ונתן" מיבעי ליה - בשלמא לדידי, מ"ונתן" לא גמרי מידי, וכולה מילתא ילפינן מ"וכחש" — דאף דלא הוי ממון להורישו לבניו ילפינן מהתם, מדגלי רחמנא גבי קרבן שבועה. אלא לדידך, דילפת מ"ונתן" דלא הוי ממונא עד שעת נתינה, ולא זכי אב אחר העמדה בדין כמו קודם — א"כ, "ונתן" מיבעי ליה, ואין צריך קרא ד"וכחש" על כך, דפשיטא דכיון דאי מודה מיפטר, פטור נמי מקרבן שבועה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 42b:12:1.english: If so, [why did it say] "the verse states 'and deal falsely'"? It should have [said] "the verse states 'shall give'" - It is well according to me, [for] from [the phrase] "shall give" we do not derive anything, and the entire matter we derive from [the phrase] "and deal falsely" — for even [the law] that it is not [considered] money to bequeath it to his children we derive from there, since the Merciful One revealed [this] regarding an oath-offering. But according to you, who derive from "shall give" that it is not [considered] money until the time of giving, and the father does not acquire [it] after standing trial just as [he does not acquire it] beforehand — if so, it should have [said] "shall give," and the verse of "and deal falsely" is not needed for this, since it is obvious that because if he admits [liability] he is exempt, he is also exempt from an oath-offering.

Tosafot on Ketubot 42b:13:1.hebrew: כי אצטריך קרא כגון שעמדה בדין ובגרה ואח"כ מתה דכי ירית מינה דידה קא ירית - ואע"ג דהשתא ממון גמור הוא, שלא בא לידו מכח קנס, ואי מודה מיחייב, אפ"ה פטור מקרבן שבועה מ"וכחש". והיינו דפריך למאי דשני השתא: "יצאו אלו שהן קנס" — ממון הוא! אבל עד השתא הוה אתי ליה שפיר דקרי ליה קנס, הואיל ובא לידו מכח קנס ואי מודה מיפטר. אבל השתא דמוקמינן לקרא בכי האי גוונא, כגון שעמדה בדין ומתה, שלא בא לידו מכח הקנס אלא מכח ירושה, ומלתא דפשיטא היא דאי מודה מיחייב — אמאי קרי ליה קנס? ומשני: תני "יצאו אלו שעיקרן קנס". והשתא, כולהו קנסות משעמד בדין ממונא הוי ומיחייב בהודאתו, ואפי' הכי גזירת הכתוב היא מ"וכחש" דפטור מקרבן שבועה. והכי נמי אפילו לר' אלעזר דאמר נשבעין על הקרקעות, גזירת הכתוב היא דפטור מקרבן שבועה, אע"ג דמיחייב בהודאתו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 42b:13:1.english: When the verse is necessary [is] in a case where she stood trial, and reached majority, and afterward died, for when [her father] inherits, he inherits from her - Even though it is now a full-fledged monetary [obligation] — as it did not come into his possession by virtue of a fine, and if he admits [liability] he is obligated [to pay] — nevertheless, he is exempt from an oath-offering based on [the verse] "and deal falsely." And this is why [the Gemara] asks regarding what [Rava] just answered: "[In the baraita it says:] 'Excluding these, as they are a fine' — [but] it is a monetary [obligation]!" Whereas until now, it worked out well for [the Gemara] that [the baraita] called it a fine, since it came into his possession by virtue of a fine and if he admits [liability] he is exempt. But now that we establish the verse in such a case — such as where she stood trial and died, where it did not come into his [i.e., the father's] possession by virtue of the fine, but rather by virtue of inheritance, and it is obvious that if [the defendant] admits [liability] he is obligated — why does [the baraita] call it a fine? And [the Gemara] answers: Teach [the baraita as], "Excluding these, whose origin is a fine." And now, all fines, once [the defendant] has stood trial, are monetary [obligations] and he is obligated [to pay] upon his own admission; nevertheless, it is a scriptural decree from "and deal falsely" that he is exempt from an oath-offering. And so too, even according to Rabbi Elazar, who says that an oath is taken regarding real property, it is a scriptural decree that one is exempt from an oath-offering, even though he is obligated [to pay] upon his own admission.

Tosafot on Ketubot 42b:15:1.hebrew: הא עמד בדין דמשלם ע"פ עצמו כו' - ולדבריו דרבה קאמר לה: בשלמא לדידי, דסבירא לי דבכל קנסות אפילו עמד בדין אינו משלם ע"פ עצמו, ולעולם חשיב קנס לרבי שמעון עד שיגיע לידו כדשמעינן מוכחש — אתי שפיר, דכל היכא דמיחייב ע"פ עצמו מיחייב נמי קרבן שבועה, כגון עמדה בדין ובגרה ומתה, דמינה ירית. אלא לדידך, הא כל קנסות שעמד בדין, או באונס ומפתה שעמדה בדין ובגרה ומתה, אף על גב דמיחייב בהודאתו פטור מקרבן שבועה — תיקשי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 42b:15:1.english: However, if he stood trial, in which case he pays on his own [admission], etc. - And [Abaye] says this according to Rabbah's own position: Granted, according to me, who holds that in all fines, even if he stood trial, he does not pay on his own [admission], and it is always considered a fine according to Rabbi Shimon until it reaches his hand, as we learn from [the verse] "and he denied" (vekhichesh) — it works out well, for wherever he is liable on his own [admission], he is also liable for an oath-offering, such as [in the case where] she stood trial, came of age (bagrah), and died, where [the father] inherits from her. But according to you — behold, [in] all fines where he stood trial, or in [the case of] a rapist or seducer where she stood trial, came of age, and died, even though he is liable through his admission, he is exempt from an oath-offering — [this] should be a difficulty.

Tosafot on Ketubot 42b:1:1.hebrew: מאי לאו בשעמד בדין - וא"ת: בשלמא לרבי יוחנן, דסגי ביחוד כלי, דסבירא ליה דמעות קונות — אתי שפיר, דאע"ג דייחד לו כלי לקנס וקני ליה, מ"מ דין קנס עליו לענין קרבן שבועה ולענין כמה דברים עד שיבא לידו. אלא לר"ל, דלא מיחייב קרבן שבועה אלא כשנטלו ממנו וחזר והפקידו אצלו — אמאי פטר ר"ש הכא? הואיל ועמד בדין ונטלו הימנו, ממון גמור הוא! ואומר רשב"א, דלריש לקיש מצי למימר דמיירי שנתן לו כלי בתורת משכון לקנסו וחזר והפקידו אצלו; דהואיל ולא נתן לו אלא בתורת משכון, לא חשיב ממון אע"פ שהיה בידו. תימה לרבינו יצחק: בהפיל את שינו וסימא את עינו, אמאי לא מיחייב קרבן שבועה? הא מתחייב בהודאתו כיון שעמד בדין ופטרוהו ב"ד ואין לו עליו כלום! ושמא, כיון דאכתי מחוסר גט שחרור, אם היה מודה שסימא את עינו לא היה יוצא לחירות:
Tosafot on Ketubot 42b:1:1.english: What, is it not [referring to a case] where he has stood trial? - And if you ask: Granted according to Rabbi Yochanan, for whom the designation of a vessel suffices—since he holds that money acquires [a movable item]—it works out well; for even though [the liable party] designated a vessel for him for the fine and he acquired it, nevertheless the status of a fine remains upon it with respect to an oath-offering and with respect to several [other] matters until it comes into his hand. However, according to Reish Lakish, [who holds] that one is only liable for an oath-offering when [the claimant] took it from him and then deposited it back with him, why does Rabbi Shimon exempt [him] here? Since he stood trial and [the claimant] took it from him, it is full-fledged money! And Rashba says that according to Reish Lakish, one can say that [the baraita] is dealing with a case where he gave him a vessel as a pledge for his fine and then deposited it back with him; for since he only gave it to him as a pledge, it is not considered [full-fledged] money even though it was in his hand. Rabbeinu Yitzchak finds [this] difficult: In [the case of one who] knocked out his [slave's] tooth or blinded his eye, why is he not liable for an oath-offering? Surely he would become liable through his admission once he stood trial and the court released [the slave], and he has no [claim] over him at all! And perhaps, since [the slave] still lacks a bill of manumission, if [the master] had admitted that he blinded his eye, [the slave] would not go free.

Tosafot on Ketubot 42b:1:2.hebrew: לא בשלא עמד בדין - וא"ת: אי בלא עמד בדין, פשיטא דלא מיחייב קרבן שבועה, דלא מידי כפריה, דאי מודה מיפטר, ומה צריך קרא ד"וכחש" לכך? והו"ל לאקשויי: ת"ל "וכחש"? "אשר ירשיעון אלהים" מיבעי ליה! כדפריך לקמן: ת"ל "וכחש"? ת"ל "ונתן" מיבעי ליה! וי"ל: דהכא לא בעי לאקשויי הכי, דאיכא למימר אסמכתא בעלמא הוא; אבל לקמן פריך שפיר: כי היכי ד"וכחש" הוה לדרשא גמורה לענין שאר קנסות, הכי נמי הוה דרשא גמורה לענין אונס ופתוי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 42b:1:2.english: No, [it refers to a case] where he has not stood trial - And if you ask: If [it is speaking of a case] where he has not stood trial, it is obvious that he is not liable [to bring] an oath-offering, since he did not deny him anything [of monetary value], as if he were to confess he would be exempt — so why is the verse "and he dealt falsely" needed for this? And [furthermore, the Gemara] should have raised the objection: [Why does the baraita say] "the verse states: 'and he dealt falsely'"? It should have [cited] "whom the judges shall condemn"! — just as it objects later on: [Why does it say] "the verse states: 'and he dealt falsely'"? It should have [said] "the verse states: 'and he shall give'"! And one can answer: Here [the Gemara] did not want to raise this objection, because one could say that [the citation] is merely a scriptural support [asmakhta]; however, later on it objects properly, [since] just as "and he dealt falsely" serves as a full-fledged exposition regarding other fines, so too it is a full-fledged exposition regarding rape and seduction.

Tosafot on Ketubot 42b:2:1.hebrew: [תשלומי כפל ותשלומי ד' וה' - ר"ש לא פליג אהא, דלא שביק איניש מידי דכי מודה מיחייב ותבע מידי דכי מודה מיפטר, דהכא הכל קייץ. מהר"מ] ת"י כ"י:
Tosafot on Ketubot 42b:2:1.english: [Double payments and fourfold and fivefold payments - Rabbi Shimon does not disagree with this — [namely, the principle] that a person does not leave aside something for which [the defendant] would be liable if he admits and claim something from which he would be exempt if he admits — for here everything is a fixed amount. Maharam.] Tosafot Yeshanim manuscript:

Tosafot on Ketubot 42b:8:1.hebrew: דאחין בעי למיהוי - בשלמא לדידי הוא קנס לכל מילי, מדגלי רחמנא לענין קרבן שבועה, אלא לדידך דאחין בעי למיהוי. תימה: וכי רבה לא ידע מתני'? ותירץ ר"י ברבי אברהם, דרבה דאמר דממון הוי להורישו לבניו — היינו כשאין הבת קיימת; אבל מתני' איירי כשהבת קיימת, דאז אין ראוי להורישו לבניו כל זמן שלא בא לידו, משום דאין אדם מוריש זכות בתו לבנו. ואביי דאקשי ליה — לא ניחא ליה לאיפלוגי בהאי, ורבה נמי הודה לו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 42b:8:1.english: It should belong to the brothers - [Abaye means:] Granted, according to me, it is a fine in all respects, since the Merciful One revealed [this] regarding an offering for an oath [of deposit]; however, according to you, it should belong to the brothers. It is astonishing: did Rabbah not know the Mishnah?! And Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Avraham answered that when Rabbah said that it is a monetary [payment] to bequeath to his sons, that is when the daughter is not alive; whereas the Mishnah is dealing with [a case] where the daughter is alive, for then it is not fit to be bequeathed to his sons as long as it has not come into his possession, because a person does not bequeath his rights in his daughter to his son. And Abaye, who raised the objection against him, did not wish to make this distinction, and Rabbah also conceded to him.
